question: On gadolinium-enhanced MRI of the internal auditory meati (IAM), a vestibular schwannoma characteristically appears as an intracanalicular or cerebellopontine-angle mass that enhances homogeneously on post-contrast T1-weighted imaging and widens the internal auditory canal.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Gadolinium enhancement is the key MRI feature of vestibular schwannoma. Small intracanalicular lesions (<1 cm) enhance brightly and are only detectable on post-contrast T1 — non-contrast MRI may miss them.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Vestibular schwannoma on contrast MRI shows homogeneous (small tumours) or heterogeneous (larger tumours) gadolinium enhancement on T1. The classic ice-cream-cone or dumbbell shape straddles the IAM fundus and the cerebellopontine angle cistern, widening the canal.
